observations: Photo 0 and 1 show a white, slim game console wrapped in clear plastic, held by a hand near a window.
A circular Xbox logo (the Xbox button) is visible on the top-left corner of the console in both photos.
The front face of the console, where a disc slot would be on a standard Xbox One S, is partly obscured by the plastic wrap and the angle of the shot.
No power brick, HDMI cable, controller, retail box, or barcode/serial label is visible in either photo.
No photo shows the console powered on or connected to a display.
Background shows unrelated items (hard drives, other electronics) in what looks like a shop/display case with 'BLESSED OBI VENTURES' watermark.

claims.claim: Microsoft Xbox One S All-Digital Edition Console (Disc-free)
claims.evidence: The Xbox logo confirms the brand/family, but the front disc-slot area that distinguishes All-Digital from standard One S is not clearly visible in either photo; plastic wrap and camera angle obscure it.

claims.claim: Implied working condition (no explicit claim, but console is being sold as a working unit)
claims.evidence: No power-on, boot screen, or controller-pairing shot is shown in either photo.

risks.risk: Cannot confirm whether this is the All-Digital Edition (no disc drive, lower market value) or a standard Xbox One S (with disc drive, higher market value) — this changes which comparable price list applies.
risks.proof: A clear, unobstructed photo of the front panel showing presence or absence of the disc slot, unwrapped.
risks.if_unproven: cannot be priced at all without this, since the model/trim itself is unreadable, not just its condition

risks.risk: Console may not power on or may have internal faults (overheating, drive failure, disc read errors if applicable).
risks.proof: A video of the console powering on to the home dashboard, or a photo of it displaying the Xbox boot logo on a screen.

risks.risk: Missing accessories (power cable, HDMI cable, controller) that are usually bundled and affect resale value.
risks.proof: A photo laying out all included accessories next to the console.

risks.risk: Storage capacity (common Xbox One S/All-Digital variants: 500GB vs 1TB) is not stated or shown, which affects price tier.
risks.proof: A photo of the rear/bottom label showing capacity, or the box if available.
risks.if_unproven: priced at the lowest common capacity tier

risks.risk: No serial number or authenticity check possible; cannot rule out a refurbished, grey-market, or modded unit.
risks.proof: A clear photo of the serial/barcode sticker, usually on the underside of the console.
risks.if_unproven: priced as unverified/grey-market risk, not premium

proof_requests: Clear, unwrapped photo of the front panel to confirm presence/absence of a disc slot.
Video of the console powering on and reaching the dashboard.
Photo of the rear/bottom label showing storage capacity and serial number.
Photo of all included accessories (cables, controller) laid out together.
response.reason: The photos confirm an Xbox-branded console but cannot settle whether it is the All-Digital Edition or a standard disc-based Xbox One S, and this model difference changes which price list applies, so even a worst-case price cannot be set without a clearer front-panel shot.
